breaks.quote: a plan so big it never left the page
breaks.why: A made-up metaphor the reader has to decode, not an image from their own life.

breaks.quote: it closes the case on her: if she just can’t, there is nothing left to try
breaks.why: A courtroom image (verdict, closing and opening the case) is a second image system the reader must decode.

breaks.quote: Even her nutritionist once told her that if she were really consistent she would see results every week
breaks.why: After Melina's story is told whole, the second half returns to it and adds a new scene, which breaks 'no new pieces of it later'.

breaks.quote: For years, that sentence ended every attempt Melina made at getting healthier.
breaks.why: This retells her story a second time after the divider instead of giving a short callback in the same words.

breaks.quote: A verdict is something you can only accept. A cause is something you can work on.
breaks.why: The passage stays with Melina's health case and the writer's own 20s, and never shows how this sentence-as-verdict pattern reaches the reader's work, money, relationships or other areas.
